slice: A26 rehearsal — live termination against the merged hardening
verdict: PASS (bundled ingest; passthrough ladder; chat/DVR/tips remain SCP-05) — after three defects found and fixed here

lab.core: two processes built from the working tree (VIDRA_ROLE=api on 127.0.0.1:8088 and VIDRA_ROLE=worker), native postgres 16 at schema 141 (migration 0141 live_termination applied), native redis on :6399, STORAGE_BACKEND=local
lab.origin: one origin on 127.0.0.1:8099 — a pipe-only proxy that drops the client's Accept-Encoding, /api/* to core and everything else to `node .next/standalone/server.js` on :3100 (never `next start`; the listener PID was checked)
lab.ingest: the compose `media` service's image run for real: alfg/nginx-rtmp pinned by digest, RepoDigests read back as alfg/nginx-rtmp@sha256:780831ae1c4116d22a287ce43f9e1befb84ccaad0b6933de041bb29b6427b513, linux/amd64 under emulation, serving the SHIPPED deploy/media/nginx.conf.template with exactly two lines changed (the shim's api upstream port 8080 -> 8088)
ingest_deviations_from_compose: the shim/control port 8082 is published to the host because core runs on the host rather than on the compose network; the compose service deliberately publishes only 1935

`--add-host api:host-gateway`, which also resolves to an IPv6 address the container cannot reach; nginx logs one failed IPv6 upstream attempt before falling back. A lab artefact of the host-gateway alias, not of the shipped compose
lab.publisher: ffmpeg 8.1, `-re -f lavfi -i testsrc2 -f lavfi -i sine -c:v libx264 -c:a aac -f flv rtmp://127.0.0.1:1935/live/<key>`, 1280x720@30 + 48 kHz AAC for the main runs, 640x360/320x180 for the short re-verifications
lab.browser: real Chromium via Playwright 1.62.1, launched with --autoplay-policy=no-user-gesture-required
lab.rate_limiting: off (RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED=false), so no 429 observation is claimed

sc1_module_truth.nginx_t_on_the_shipped_template: syntax is ok / test is successful

stat.conclusion: rtmp_stat is compiled in; /control and /stat parse, so rtmp_control is too

control_drop_nonexistent_name.note: NOT 404 on this build — the module answers 200 with the number dropped. HTTPIngestController treats any 2xx as success, so ErrIngestNoPublisher is unreachable here and publisher_disconnected can be true when nothing was dropped

defect_1_control_never_reached_the_publi.severity: blocking — the headline promise of the hardening
defect_1_control_never_reached_the_publi.mechanism: nginx-rtmp's rtmp_control and rtmp_stat are PER WORKER. Under the shipped `worker_processes auto` the streamer's RTMP session lives on one worker and the api's control request is accepted by another, where it matches nothing; the module answers 200 with a body of "0", which DropPublisher reads as success.

measured_before.after_a_real_moderator_termination: publisher kept writing for the full 60 s watched: 17 new .ts segments appeared and the .flv grew 25.8 MB -> 38.3 MB
measured_before.stat_split: consecutive fresh connections answered from different workers: pid 11 reported the packaging stream, pid 13 reported an empty server, and the worker holding the streamer's own socket answered neither

measured_after.stat: both sessions on every read, one pid

defect_1_control_never_reached_the_publi.fix: vidra-core #211 — deploy/media/nginx.conf.template `worker_processes 1;` + a test that reads the shipped template

defect_2_terminate_audit_row_was_never_w.severity: the moderation trail for the new control
defect_2_terminate_audit_row_was_never_w.mechanism: internal/audit's envelope refuses an event carrying a resource id with no resource type, and internal/live discards Record's error on purpose. content.live.terminate set ResourceID and no ResourceType, so normalizeEvent rejected it and the row vanished with no log line.
defect_2_terminate_audit_row_was_never_w.measured_before: a real termination landed every other effect (state, key rotation, publisher drop, creator-visible reason) and audit_log held only content.live.replay
defect_2_terminate_audit_row_was_never_w.why_the_unit_tests_passed: the package's fakeAuditor appended to a slice and never ran the envelope; it now pushes every event through a real audit.Service

defect_3_the_moderator_dialog_could_not_.severity: blocking — the control was unreachable from the UI
defect_3_the_moderator_dialog_could_not_.mechanism: lib/api/client.ts JSON-encodes every non-FormData body; endpoints.ts terminateLiveStream stringified its body first, so the payload was a JSON string containing JSON and echo's Bind refused it before Validate ran
defect_3_the_moderator_dialog_could_not_.measured_before: POST /api/v1/admin/live/{id}/terminate -> 400 malformed or invalid request body, body on the wire: "{\"reason_code\":\"policy_violation\",\"reason\":\"...\"}"
defect_3_the_moderator_dialog_could_not_.scope: the only endpoint in endpoints.ts that double-encoded

findings_open: DropPublisher cannot distinguish a real disconnect from 'nothing matched': this module build answers both with 200, differing only in a body count that is discarded. With one worker the honest cases coincide, but a termination of a hook-only phantom session (no publisher at all) still reports publisher_disconnected: true. Whether termination should verify the drop is a ruling

the live watch page polls only while the stream is `offline`, so during a broadcast the viewer count is a single load-time snapshot and a terminated stream does not flip to its ended state without a reload

liveViewerDigest's signed-in branch is unreachable on a public stream — hls.js sends no session credential with the playlist, so every viewer is digested by IP and viewers sharing an address count once
an owner's POST /live/{id}/end writes no audit row of any kind
content.live.replay and content.live.force_close still leave resource_id empty (deliberate, per the hardening slice)
the duration watchdog still does not use the control surface: an over-limit publisher stays connected and keeps writing segments and a recording after the cut
content.live.terminate records actor_kind=user but leaves actor_role empty
a hook-only flip still advertises a byte-less stream on the public Live-now rail
no live ABR ladder and nothing resyncs a drifted player to the live edge (SCP-05)
not_run: OBS or any real streaming client (ffmpeg was the publisher)
the compose `media` profile brought up as a profile — the service's image, command and shipped template were reproduced by hand
the hourly recording-retention ticker itself (its selection was run directly)
TLS, real hostnames, an ingest reachable from another machine
more than three concurrent viewers, and any viewer on a real remote network
teardown: every process, the postgres cluster, the Redis server and the ingest container were started by this session in a scratch directory and stopped at the end; the one instance-settings override made during the lab (live_max_duration_secs) was removed so instance_settings is empty again; credentials, stream keys, recordings, replays and raw logs stay outside the repo
